title: Set out each room's first floor tile so no border cut is under half a tile
instruction: Each room has its two centre lines chalked in blue. In each room, lay the room's loose tile flat at the crossing of the centre lines as the first tile of the floor, square to the walls, and for each line either centred on it or with a joint on it, whichever leaves the cut tiles at both walls across that line at least half a tile wide. Tiles are 60 mm with 2 mm joints. The left room is 278 mm front to back and 340 mm wide; the right room is 340 mm front to back and 278 mm wide.
context: Tile and stone setters (O*NET 47-2044.00) set a floor out from the room's centre lines: two chalk lines through the middle of the room, then a dry run of tiles to the walls. If the run would leave thin slivers at the walls, they move the start by half a tile, putting a joint on the line instead of a tile's centre, so that the cut tiles at opposite walls are equal and at least half a tile wide; slivers look bad, break when cut and come loose. Each direction is decided from the room's size across that line. With 300 mm tiles and 10 mm joints, a 1.70 m room set out with a tile centred on its line ends in 70 mm slivers at both walls; with a joint on the line both cuts are 225 mm. Here, at 1:5, two 1.70 x 1.39 m rooms turned opposite ways need opposite answers, and the first tile laid in each carries both decisions.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and is the floor of both rooms. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:5 scale model of two rooms' floors, one in front of each arm. Three kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Walls: eight fixed white-painted wooden strips, 10 mm thick and 25 mm tall, standing on the table as two rectangular rooms. Left room: inside faces at x 15.0 and 42.8 cm and at y +7.0 and +41.0 cm, so it is 278 mm front to back (along x) and 340 mm side to side (along y); its near and far walls run from y +6.0 to +42.0 cm and its two side walls fit between them. Right room: inside faces at x 12.0 and 46.0 cm and at y -34.8 and -7.0 cm, so it is 340 mm front to back and 278 mm side to side; its near and far walls run from y -35.8 to -6.0 cm. The two rooms' inner walls are 12 cm apart across the midline (outside faces at y +6.0 and -6.0 cm). (2) Chalk lines: four fixed blue plastic strips standing for snapped chalk lines, 4 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick, glued to the table, each running wall to wall through the middle of its room; positions below are their centre lines. Left room: the front-to-back line along x at y +24.0 cm (x 15.0 to 42.8 cm) and the side-to-side line along y at x 28.9 cm (y +7.0 to +41.0 cm), crossing at x 28.9, y +24.0 cm. Right room: the front-to-back line at y -20.9 cm (x 12.0 to 46.0 cm) and the side-to-side line at x 29.0 cm (y -34.8 to -7.0 cm), crossing at x 29.0, y -20.9 cm. (3) Floor tiles: two loose unglazed terracotta quarry tiles, each 60 x 60 mm and 10 mm thick, 80 g, with flat faces; a tile's two 60 x 60 mm faces are alike. Each lies flat on the floor of its room, away from the crossing and turned off square: the left room's tile centred at x 20.5 cm, y +33.5 cm, its edges turned 20 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from the walls; the right room's tile centred at x 19.5 cm, y -27.5 cm, turned 25 degrees clockwise. Each tile is 84 mm or more from its room's side-to-side line and at least 16 mm from every wall. At 1:5 the tiles and joints stand for 300 mm tiles with 10 mm joints (a 62 mm module here) and the rooms for 1.70 x 1.39 m rooms. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the tiles' poses (in a real trial: a ruler from each chalk line's centre to the tile's edges, and a top photo). A tile is 'at a room's crossing' when its centre is within 45 mm of both of that room's centre lines; tiles elsewhere are ignored, and either tile may be used in either room. A tile is 'laid' when its 60 x 60 mm faces are within 5 degrees of level (either face up), its edges are within 5 degrees of square to the walls, its lowest point is within 2 mm of the floor (the table top), and it is still (no corner moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s). For each centre line, the scorer extends the laid tile's grid of 60 mm tiles and 2 mm joints across that line to the two walls parallel to it and takes the 'border cut' at each: the gap from the last whole tile to the wall, less one 2 mm joint, which is (D/2 - u - 32 mm) and (D/2 + u - 32 mm), each reduced modulo 62 mm, where D is the room's inside size across the line and u the distance of the tile's centre from the line. That direction is 'right' when both cuts are at least 30 mm (half a tile). This works out as: with 278 mm of room across the line, the tile's centre within 15 mm of the line (centred on it: cuts 45 and 45 mm); with 340 mm across it, the centre 16 mm or more from the line, on either side (a joint on the line, centre 31 mm from it: cuts 45 and 45 mm). Centred on a 340 mm line, or with a joint on a 278 mm line, the cuts are 14 and 14 mm. So the left room needs a joint on its front-to-back line and a tile centred on its side-to-side line, and the right room the opposite. Each room scores 0.5 when exactly one tile is at its crossing and that tile is laid with both directions right. Otherwise the room scores 0: no tile at its crossing (left where it started, or its centre more than 45 mm from either line, e.g. on a right grid one module further out), both tiles at its crossing, or the tile there tilted more than 5 degrees or on an edge, turned more than 5 degrees from square (e.g. laid diagonally), not within 2 mm of the floor (held up, or fallen off the table), still moving, or set out wrong in either direction. The score is the sum of the two rooms. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Examples: both tiles centred on the crossings, 0; a joint on every line, 0; the left room's answer copied into the right room, 0.5; both rooms right, 1.0. The trial ends early, at 1.0, once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit (a 1.0 state there counts even if it has held less than 2 s). The scorer reads only the tiles, not the grippers: a tile still held is scored where it lies.
fidelity: About 1:5 scale. Rigid boxes with default friction; walls and lines are fixed. Tiles are 10 mm thick so a gripper can hold them (1:5 of a 10 mm tile is 2 mm). Lines are 4 mm wide so the camera shows them; offsets are measured to their centres. They are 0.5 mm proud, so a tile laid across one sits about 1 degree off level. No adhesive, spacers or perimeter gap; cuts are measured to the wall faces. A setter dry-lays rows both ways; here the scorer extends the first tile's grid.
reset_notes: Put the left room's tile back flat on the floor centred at x 20.5 cm, y +33.5 cm, its edges turned 20 degrees anticlockwise from the walls (seen from above), and the right room's tile centred at x 19.5 cm, y -27.5 cm, turned 25 degrees clockwise. The walls and chalk lines are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
